A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fingerprintability is not a binary property of browsers, but rather a spectrum, and that the choice of a browser can significantly affect an Internet user's level of anonymity and privacy.
the fingerprintability of a browser depends on its version, its platform and its configuration, and that it can vary by orders of magnitude between browsers and platforms.
fingerprinting potential is a property that varies significantly between browsers, and that the choice of a browser can have a significant impact on the privacy of a user.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the most privacy-friendly browser is not a trivial one.
the fingerprinting potential of browsers is a significant and under-appreciated privacy concern, and that the fingerprinting of browsers should be considered a serious threat to privacy.
